A Guy With A Scarf research/Automated match video/Premium edition/Min Fotboll (Svenska Fotbollförbundet)

Distribution layer, club and viewer split · adjacent platform

Min Fotboll (Svenska Fotbollförbundet)Premium

Solna, Sweden · founded 2018 · active · www.svenskfotboll.se/serier-cuper/min-fotboll · last verified 2026-09-19

Distribution layer, club and viewer splitSoftware onlyNo Italian presence foundEvidence AViewer pays

Min Fotboll is the Swedish FA's official app, in which volunteers stream matches from a phone or a connected Veo or Spiideo camera and viewers pay SEK 59 for 30 days of every youth match in Sweden, with half the revenue after VAT going to a club of the viewer's choice minfotboll-01, minfotboll-02.

For Every Swedish club, from children's teams to lower senior divisions, since the app is free to use, tied to the FA's competition database and the only place SvFF sanctions youth streaming minfotboll-01, minfotboll-03. Families and grandparents who want to follow a child's team anywhere in the country are the paying audience minfotboll-01.

Min Fotboll exists because the Swedish FA decided that grassroots streaming, sponsorship and communication should sit inside one federation-owned app, away from fragmented commercial platforms, and it framed GDPR control as a reason from the start minfotboll-03, minfotboll-04. It matters now because it is the clearest example of a federation owning the distribution and checkout layer and treating camera vendors such as Veo and Spiideo as interchangeable inputs, with nearly 11,500 livestreams and 126,000 matches with user content in 2024 minfotboll-01, minfotboll-05. It tells you that where a federation moves first, the automated camera becomes a peripheral and the pricing power moves to the app that holds the fixtures minfotboll-02, minfotboll-06.

Price band Free for clubs; youth viewer pass SEK 59 per 30 days for all youth matches; senior PPV set by the club; club replay package SEK 2,000 per year; 50 percent of revenue after VAT to the chosen club minfotboll-01

Italy Min Fotboll is a Swedish federation service available only for Swedish competitions and has no presence outside Sweden minfotboll-01, minfotboll-03.

The verdict

Look if You are a Swedish club, because the app is free, sanctioned by the FA, integrated with fixtures and the only route to paid youth streaming in the country minfotboll-01, minfotboll-03. You should also look if you are a federation elsewhere studying how to own grassroots distribution, since the SEK 59 nationwide youth pass with viewer-directed revenue is a model no commercial platform offers minfotboll-01.

Skip if You are outside Sweden, since the service has no international scope minfotboll-03. You should also skip it as a coaching tool, since the replay package is a SEK 2,000 add-on and the app carries no analysis features minfotboll-01.

Watch-outs

  • Youth streams are sold as a single SEK 59 nationwide pass, so an individual club's income depends on viewers choosing it at checkout, independent of the size of its own audience minfotboll-01.
  • Streaming is done by volunteers and the FA itself asks viewers for understanding on connection and quality problems, so consistency varies by team minfotboll-01.
  • Camera streaming into the app depends on integration partners, with Veo Cam 2 integration announced in November 2022 and Spiideo scheduling documented in Spiideo's help centre, and the FA controls which vendors are admitted minfotboll-06, minfotboll-07.
  • The App Store rating is 4.2 from about 1,500 reviews, and the privacy label lists user content, identifiers, usage and advertising data linked to the user minfotboll-08.

Company

Ownership and funding Min Fotboll is owned and operated by Svenska Fotbollförbundet, the Swedish Football Association, which is the app's publisher on the App Store and states that all economic surplus is returned to districts and clubs minfotboll-03, minfotboll-08.

Financials not public; the FA states that the app's surplus goes back to districts and clubs and reported SEK 1.2 million paid to clubs through the app by October 2020 minfotboll-03, minfotboll-09.

Scale, company-stated Nearly 900,000 downloads, 126,000 matches with user-generated content and almost 11,500 livestreams in 2024, as stated by SvFF on 29 April 2025 minfotboll-05. 600,000 users in April 2023 and 350,000 monthly active users in 2022 minfotboll-03. 570,000 users and about 1,000 active Veo cameras in Sweden at the November 2022 Veo partnership minfotboll-06.

Partnerships

  • Veo, partnership announced 25 November 2022 with discounted cameras for Swedish clubs and direct streaming from Veo Cam 2 into Min Fotboll minfotboll-06.
  • Spiideo, cooperation announced August 2021 with broadcast scheduling to Min Fotboll documented in Spiideo's help centre minfotboll-07, minfotboll-10.

2025 and 2026

  • 2025-04-29: SvFF publishes usage figures of nearly 900,000 downloads, 126,000 matches with content and 11,500 livestreams in 2024 and lists what clubs can do in the app minfotboll-05.
  • 2025-09-01: App version 3.1.9 released on the App Store minfotboll-08.

Not verified

  • Exact launch year: SvFF's April 2023 article says five years earlier, UEFA's 2022 article says the app launched ahead of the 2020 season, so 2018 for the app and 2020 for streaming is the best reading.
  • Total revenue paid to clubs from livestreaming since 2020.
  • Whether Veo Cam 3 and other current camera models are integrated, since the FA page names Veo and Spiideo without model detail.
  • Senior match PPV price ranges, which clubs set individually.
